title: Kariobangi Sharks, Mombasa United Agree to October Playoff
desc: Kariobangi Sharks and Mombasa United will face off in a two-leg playoff after reaching an agreement through FKF mediation.
content:
Kariobangi Sharks and Mombasa United have agreed to settle their promotion and relegation dispute through a two-legged playoff after talks mediated by the Football Kenya Federation (FKF) on Thursday, September 24.

The agreement provides a route for the two clubs to determine who will occupy the contested FKF Premier League place after weeks of legal and administrative uncertainty surrounding the start of the 2026/27 season.

The first leg will be played in Mombasa on October 1, with the return match scheduled for Nairobi on October 6. Both clubs have also agreed to field their newly registered players in the two matches.

The breakthrough follows a dispute over the regulations governing promotion and relegation at the end of the 2025/26 season. Kariobangi Sharks finished 16th in the Premier League, while Mombasa United finished third in the National Super League (NSL).

The application of different FKF regulatory frameworks became the centre of the dispute, with the matter subsequently reaching the courts. The uncertainty contributed to the postponement of the 2026/27 Premier League season, which had been scheduled to begin on September 19.

FKF had called the clubs for mediation as it sought a way through the impasse. The talks have now produced an agreement that moves the dispute from administrative and legal channels to the football pitch.

For Kariobangi Sharks, the playoff provides an opportunity to retain their place in Kenya's top flight. Mombasa United, meanwhile, will be seeking to secure a Premier League place after their third-place finish in the NSL.

The decision on player eligibility was also significant. Both sides will be permitted to use players registered for the new season, removing one of the practical difficulties that had complicated efforts to organise the playoff.

The two matches will now determine the immediate top-flight fate of the clubs, while also providing FKF with a clearer path toward resolving the uncertainty that has delayed the new Premier League campaign.

With the agreement reached, attention now shifts to the October 1 first leg in Mombasa before the return fixture in Nairobi five days later.
